page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-2 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the arm64 architecture, the instance provides an elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The server configuration includes no integrated GPU accelerators and contains no local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for operating system and application volumes.

The hardware configuration trades compute density for increased memory capacity per virtual core. Software deployments must be compatible with the 64-bit Arm instruction set. Because local disk devices and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included, storage architectures and external networking configurations depend entirely on external cloud resources.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides resource efficiency for memory-sensitive environments without the overhead of unused compute cores. Appropriate deployment scenarios include lightweight in-memory caching tiers, small relational databases, staging buffers, and background data services optimized for the Arm architecture.
